subject: Priority mosaic and open probes — MedSync bakeoff
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Priority mosaic and open probes — MedSync bakeoff

Samir — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have one source of truth.

Quick recap (what you told us)
- Primary pain: unpredictable tail latency during batch ingestion windows (p95 spikes from ~200ms to >1s).
- Cost sensitivity: need predictable token/unit economics at scale — current model costs are a blocker for enterprise purchase.
- Compliance: data residency and auditability are gating for production, plus SOC2 evidence.
- Deployment preference: want an option that can live in a VPC or dedicated pool to isolate PHI ingestion.

Goals we agreed on
1) Validate latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms on 256-token prompts under target load.
2) Surface predictable monthly cost envelope for your busiest workload.
3) Demonstrate private-deployment (VPC) parity + audit logs for a short pilot.

Proposed technical probes (scope for bakeoff)
- Probe A — Latency/stability: 30-minute sustained run at your peak QPS with 256-token prompts, measure p50/p95/p99 and cold-start behavior.
- Probe B — Failover & graceful degradation: force a model variant fallback during load (quantized model) and measure throughput and quality delta on your evaluation prompts.
- Probe C — Residency & audit: replay a small redacted sample of your ingestion flow into a VPC sandbox and confirm audit log fidelity and retention.

Open questions we need answered to schedule the tests
- Do you have a small redacted dataset (5–10k rows) we can use for the residency test? If yes, what format?
- Which region(s) do you want us to run the latency probe in (us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1)?
- Will procurement want a PO template or MSA in advance?

Immediate next steps
1) We’ll share a focused test matrix (CSV) with probe definitions and acceptance criteria by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you can share the redacted sample and a short prioritized prompt list, we’ll schedule the latency run for the week of Nov 8.
3) Camila (cc’d) will surface any competitive observations and propose a minimal set of A/B probe variants.

Attachments: priority-mosaic-v1.pdf (one-page priority map), call-recording-link.txt (link to call recording)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the test matrix and timeline.

— Vanessa Ortiz

- Sample format: we can provide a CSV extract with columns [patient_id (hashed), payload_text, timestamp, doc_type]. We will redact PHI fields before sharing.

- Please add a data-residency probe to confirm that logs and KV cache never leave the selected region. That’s a hard requirement for our security team.
- Procurement (looping in Jenny) will need a draft PO and an outline of data handling for legal review.

Timing
- A short tech deep-dive next Tue or Wed (Nov 2/3) would work for our engineering and security leads.

Thanks — I’ve copied Jenny from procurement to coordinate contracts.

— Samir

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Competitive notes + suggested A/B probes (internal only)

Vanessa / Marissa — internal thoughts after the call, comparing MedSync priorities to recent bakeoffs. Leaving this on-thread so we keep context.

Driver: MedSync is very focused on tail latency under specific batch loads and on-region residency. That combination narrows our sweet spot to: dedicated pools with prefix/KV caching + regional routing.

Competitor notes (quick)
- OrbitAI: strong on cost (dense quantization options) but historically worse at p95 under burst because of cache misses on multi-tenant shared pools.
- CloudServe AI: good at VPC/on-prem packaging but their telemetry/audit logs are coarse — legal teams push back.

Suggested A/B probes to include in the test-matrix (minimally intrusive)
A. Baseline run (shared-hosted variant) — measure baseline p50/p95 and token-cost. Owner: Vanessa
B. Dedicated pool + prefix caching — evaluate p95 improvement and cost delta. Owner: Camila
C. Quantized fallback variant (simulate node failover) — measure quality regression & time-to-failover. Owner: Marissa
D. Residency check: run identical ingestion in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with logs shipped to region-specific storage; validate log hashes and retention. Owner: Camila

Notes on success criteria (internal)
- Win if p95 improves >= 2x vs baseline without >25% cost increase.
- Residency: logs must be demonstrably region-local (hash diff + metadata) and accessible to their auditors for 30 days.

I’ll prepare short runbooks for B and C this week and stitch them into the test-matrix. If we want to be conservative on risk, start with a non-production bucket for the residency probe.

— Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
